transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date/Time: 2027-03-30 15:00 UTC
- Duration: 48 minutes
- Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Daniel Kim (Redwood SE), Olivia Hernandez (CTO, SignalPath), Marcus Lee (Lead Platform Eng), Priya Nair (SRE), Samir Gupta (Head of Product)

Summary:
Quick discovery focused on p95 latency targets for streaming and non-streaming paths, expected concurrency during peak tokenstorms, and whether SignalPath should go Hosted, Dedicated, or Private for their use case. Caller asked about token/sec benchmarks, cold start impact, and security requirements. Agreed to run a joint benchmark.

Topics covered:
- Workload characterization: short chat replies (8-40 tokens) + longer summarization (400-1k tokens)
- p95 targets: 200-400ms for short-turn streaming, 800-1200ms for long-form completion p95
- Concurrency: steady 120 concurrent users, bursts to 800 concurrent sessions for 30s windows
- Token throughput: average 600 tokens/sec sustained, burst 3k tokens/sec across tenant
- Hosting path decision factors: data residency, KMS/HSM, audit logs, SSO/SAML, and observability

Action items (captured here and in metadata): see action_items field

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya: hey everyone, thanks for joining. olivia, samir — thanks for making time. we'll do a quick intro then jump into traffic profile, p95 targets, and hosting path.
[00:15] Olivia: mm thanks. short background — SignalPath is a realtime event analysis platform, we do live summarization of user sessions and then deep act actions. latency is our biggest concern, p95 ideally under 300ms for the quick answers.
[00:30] Marcus: yeah i want to add that we have two main flows: interactive chat (8-40 tokens) and batch summarization where sequences can go up to 1k tokens. the interactive flow is what the front-line UX cares about.
[00:45] Daniel: got it. for interactive are you expecting streaming token-by-token responses or complete-response style?
[00:50] Priya: streaming for interactive, definitely. we measure p95 on first-token latency and also on completion for the longer ones.
[01:10] Maya: helpful. can you give ballpark concurrent users during peak? you mentioned spikes earlier in the doc.
[01:18] Samir: steady state about 120 concurrent sessions, but during product events we see spikes up to 800 concurrent for 20-40 seconds, then it settles. token rates jump too — maybe 3k tokens/sec for the burst window.
[01:36] Daniel: okay that pattern maps to two needs: a low-latency streaming path for the interactive flow and a high-throughput path for the batch summaries. Redwood can route by policy to different model variants or hardware.
[01:52] Olivia: can you clarify hosted vs dedicated latency characteristics? we've tested openAI and sometimes the hosted routes hit unpredictable tail latencies.
[02:03] Maya: yeah, so Hosted gives fastest time-to-value, but shared capacity means you can see variance in p95 during noisy neighbour events. Dedicated is reserved GPU pools — you get predictable throughput and much tighter p95 profiles, plus better latency SLAs. Private (VPC / on-prem) is for when you need full network isolation and KMS integration.
[02:30] Marcus: are there numbers you can share for p95 on, say, a 13B-ish open model and a 70B-ish model on dedicated infra?
[02:38] Daniel: rough numbers for Redwood Dedicated on modern A100-like hardware — for short streaming prompts (<=40 tokens) p95 first token we often see 120-250ms depending on quantization and batching; for 70B it might be 200-400ms. For large completions the completion p95 can be 600-1200ms for 1k tokens depending on token generation speed. this is workload dependent.
[03:05] Priya: you mentioned quantization — that hurts output quality sometimes. how do you recommend balancing latency vs quality?
[03:12] Daniel: good question. we advise model/quantization per workload. interactive short replies can tolerate more aggressive quant (int8/4bit) where quality impact is minimal; long-form summarization we often run on fp16/amp or lightly quantized variants. Redwood Optimize gives recommendations per prompt set.
[03:36] Olivia: curious about batching — automatic batching can introduce latency. how does that work for streaming?
[03:43] Maya: Redwood uses continuous batching and has knobs: for low-latency streams we set small batch windows and prioritize latency SLO, for high-throughput background jobs we allow larger batch sizes to improve token/sec. there's an autoscaler that adjusts based on request patterns.
[04:02] Samir: and cache? we do a lot of prefix reuse — can caching reduce cost and latency?
[04:07] Daniel: yes, prefix/KV cache can drastically reduce per-token compute — we saw 30-60% token cost reductions on workloads with high prefix reuse. but caching behavior depends on how you pin or route models and the sequences; also eviction patterns matter.
[04:28] Priya: security — we need KMS integration and audit logs. what's available in Private mode vs Hosted?
[04:34] Maya: Hosted supports customer-managed keys via KMS integration in the nearline offering, but for strict compliance Private (VPC) or on-prem gives you full control over keys and network. we provide audit logs and SSO via SAML/Okta and RBAC. we can share SOC2 and penetration test reports.
[04:58] Olivia: awesome — yes send the security pack.
[05:02] Marcus: back on p95, our SLO for the product is p95 < 300ms for interactive replies, else we get user complaints. is that realistic with Dedicated?
[05:11] Daniel: yes Dedicated is the path to hit that consistently. with right model size, quant, and batching controls Dedicated with reserved GPUs and tuned kernel selection can get you into that window. we'll need to validate with your prompts and real sequence lengths.
[05:29] Samir: what's the cold start behavior? during a spike to 800 conc we may scale up new workers — how much time to add capacity?
[05:35] Daniel: scale depends on target infra; for Dedicated we recommend reserved baseline capacity sized for typical steady state and then burst to reserved extra or shared pool. cold start to spin up new GPUs can be minutes, so autoscale uses pre-warmed pools and fast failover to lower-latency variants. there's also model warm caching for KV so new replicas can bring checkpoint faster.
[05:58] Priya: could you run an experiment that simulates our 800-concurrent, 30s spike to 3k tokens/sec and measure p95 for interactive and completion?
[06:05] Maya: absolutely — that'll be part of the joint benchmark. Daniel will own the harness.
[06:10] Daniel: yeah i'll set up a benchmark harness that can replay token distributions and concurrent sessions. want me to include streaming-first-token and streaming-completion p95s, plus tail latency percentiles?
[06:21] Olivia: yes please, include p50/p95/p99 and token/sec sustained and burst. also instrument network hop times and app-side queuing so we can separate infra vs application latency.
[06:36] Samir: do you have example telemetry we can share so our observability team plugs into Redwood Console?
[06:41] Maya: we'll share the dashboard templates and tracing hooks — Console provides per-route breakdowns with token-level cost and latency. also you can add tracing headers to correlate spans.
[06:55] Marcus: one more thing: we sometimes fan-out a single user request to multiple model calls and then reduce. that increases token/s and concurrency at the backend. graph is complex. will that be a problem?
[07:05] Daniel: it's common. Redwood supports smart routing and multiplexing. best practice is to pipeline and where possible use multi-call batching on the server. we can simulate your fanout pattern in the benchmark.
[07:18] Olivia: what's the easiest way to test Dedicated without committing to a year contract? we want to validate performance first.
[07:25] Maya: we offer a short pilot — typically 6-12 weeks — with reserved capacity and a reduced commit so you can run the benchmarks and a small production pilot. we'll include rollback/route-based fallbacks during the pilot.
[07:40] Samir: cost question: how does token cost change when we move from Hosted shared pools to Dedicated?
[07:45] Daniel: unit cost on Dedicated is lower per-token because of reserved hardware economics, but you pay for reserved capacity. so if you have steady baseline that fits reservations, it often lowers cost; for variable bursts Hosted or shared pools can sometimes be cheaper if you don't want reservation. we'll model your traffic in the cost calc.
[08:02] Priya: wondering about model variants — can we pin a small model for interactive and a larger for summaries?
[08:09] Maya: yes you can route by policy — route short prompts to a smaller, faster model; long summarizations go to a larger one. Redwood can fallback if larger model capacity isn't available.
[08:22] Marcus: test specifics: our interactive median tokens is 18 tokens, 95th is 38 tokens. long jobs average 520 tokens. can you size based on that?
[08:31] Daniel: that's great data. i'll use those distributions for the benchmark. also need top-100 prompts for quality checks since quantization can affect generation.
[08:42] Olivia: we use internal privacy constraints — no PII leaves our VPC. does Redwood support Private deployments inside customer VPCs?
[08:49] Maya: yes Private VPC is supported — control plane still managed but data plane in your VPC; for fully air-gapped on-prem we have an on-prem package. both support KMS and HSM integrations.
[09:03] Samir: what about observability retention — our ops team wants 90 days of traces. is that an add-on?
[09:09] Daniel: observability retention is configurable; extended retention is an add-on. we'll include options in the pilot pricing.
[09:18] Priya: curious about network topology — we'll have cross-AZ traffic if it's hosted. any routing best practices?
[09:23] Maya: recommend colocating inference capacity in your primary region to minimize hop. For Dedicated we can provision in the region you choose and use private peering.
[09:34] Marcus: on benchmark - do you run on A100s or newer? we want to compare to our in-house Triton setup on H100.
[09:40] Daniel: we run on a variety of hardware; Dedicated can be provisioned on A100/H100-equivalent. kernel selection and compilation differences mean H100 may have better throughput for some models. we'll mirror your hardware where possible for apples-to-apples.
[09:59] Olivia: what's the expected p95 for first token when streaming for our 18-token median if we use a 13B optimized on H100?
[10:06] Daniel: rough estimate: 13B on H100, first-token p95 for streaming could be ~90-180ms with minimal batching and good network placement — but we'll measure to confirm.
[10:20] Samir: we need explicit tail numbers — p99 matter to us (we want p99 < 1s ideally). can you test p99 too?
[10:27] Daniel: yes we'll collect p50/p95/p99.
[10:31] Priya: any gotchas about tokenization differences across models? we sometimes see token counts change and affect throughput assumptions.
[10:38] Daniel: tokenize variations are real — we'll use your exact tokenizer or the same model tokenizer in the harness so numbers align.
[10:48] Maya: ok quick pause — are there any hard constraints on data residency or certification besides SOC2?
[10:55] Olivia: gdpr region data residency for EU customers; also FedRAMP is not required now but may be in future.
[11:03] Maya: noted. we'll surface region availability for the pilot.
[11:08] Marcus: let's talk about failure modes — if a model replica OOMs during peak, do you have automated fallback?
[11:15] Daniel: yes, Redwood has fallback policies: route to a compatible smaller model or route to a lower-cost variant. we can configure automatic retries and canary rollouts to avoid broad impact.
[11:31] Samir: would that degrade quality noticeably?
[11:34] Daniel: depends on how different the fallback model is; we try to pick compatible family variants to preserve output. we'll include quality regression checks in the benchmark.
[11:45] Priya: on instrumentation — can we export metrics via Prometheus?
[11:49] Maya: yes metrics export via Prometheus is supported for Dedicated and Private; Hosted has telemetry ingestion into Console and can forward via exporters.
[11:59] Olivia: okay next — scheduling. when can we run the benchmark?
[12:02] Maya: we can kick off the harness next week pending prompt sets and sample traffic. daniel — earliest slot?
[12:09] Daniel: I can start setting up Friday, run the first sweep the following Tuesday. it'll be a full day of runs to capture steady and spike windows.
[12:17] Marcus: good. please include streaming-first-token, streaming-completion p95, completion p95 for long jobs, and a separate run that simulates our fanout pattern.
[12:27] Daniel: will do.
[12:31] Samir: what telemetry do you need from our side?
[12:35] Priya: sample prompts, token distribution, peak schedule, and any client-side timeout settings.
[12:41] Maya: and access to a test environment IP allowlist if we do private peering for the pilot.
[12:48] Olivia: we'll assemble that this week.
[12:51] Priya: one more thing: quantization regressions — can you run A/B quality checks? we have some subjective quality criteria.
[12:58] Daniel: yes we'll include A/B evals on the top-100 prompts and flag any degrade beyond your acceptance threshold.
[13:06] Maya: wrapping up — recap/outcomes and next steps.
[13:09] Maya: Redwood to run joint benchmark simulating steady 120 conc, burst 800 conc (30s), token distributions, and fanout pattern. collect p50/p95/p99, token/sec sustained and burst, quality A/B for top-100 prompts. Redwood to share security docs and pilot pricing. SignalPath to provide prompts, token stats, and a whitelist for testing.
[13:30] Olivia: sounds good.
[13:33] Samir: couple of micro details: please include expected cost per token estimates for both Hosted and Dedicated in the follow-up.
[13:39] Maya: yes that'll be in the pricing email.
[13:42] Marcus: thanks, that's helpful.
[13:45] Priya: thanks everyone.
[13:49] Maya: we'll follow up with calendar invites for the benchmark kickoff. thanks all.

[47:30] (call ended)
